\textbf{(a)} Differentiate $x^2-4xy+8y^2=1$ (product rule on $4xy$):
\[2x-4y-4xy'+16yy'=0\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4y-2x}{16y-4x}=\frac{2y-x}{8y-2x}.\]
\textbf{(b)} Parallel to $x+y=1$ means slope $-1$: $2y-x=-(8y-2x)\Rightarrow 10y=3x\Rightarrow y=\frac{3x}{10}$. Substitute:
\[x^2-\tfrac{12}{10}x^2+\tfrac{72}{100}x^2=0.52x^2=1\ \Rightarrow\ x=\pm\frac{5}{\sqrt{13}}.\]
One point: \boxed{\Big(\tfrac{5}{\sqrt{13}},\ \tfrac{3}{2\sqrt{13}}\Big)} (the other is its negative).

\textbf{(c)} At $P=(1,\frac12)$ (check: $1-2+2=1$): $y'=\dfrac{1-1}{4-2}=\boxed{0}$.

\textbf{(d)} Differentiate $y'=\dfrac{2y-x}{8y-2x}$ with the quotient rule:
\[y''=\frac{(2y'-1)(8y-2x)-(2y-x)(8y'-2)}{(8y-2x)^2}.\]
At $P$: $y'=0$ and $2y-x=0$, so $y''=\dfrac{(-1)(2)-0}{2^2}=\boxed{-\tfrac12}$.
